title: He wasn’t ruined.
paragraphs:
He wasn’t ruined.
He was repositioned.

Because if you only see Joseph on his knees in chains…
you’ll miss what God was doing behind the scenes.

If you only see betrayal…
you’ll never recognize divine strategy wrapped in pain.
Some of you feel like that right now.
You did right… and still got hurt.
You trusted… and still got betrayed.
You stayed faithful… and still got forgotten.
And deep inside, there’s a whisper:
But Joseph’s story confronts that lie.
He was hated by his own blood.

Stripped of his robe.
Thrown into a pit.
Sold like property.
Imagine the silence in that hole.

No applause.
No explanation.
No rescue.
Just darkness… and the echo of betrayal.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

He didn’t block the brothers.
He didn’t send angels.
He didn’t interrupt the sale.

Because if God is good…
why allow that level of pain?
Here’s the tension most people avoid:
God is not absent in your suffering.
He is active in a way you don’t yet understand.
“You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive…” — Genesis 50:20
Some scholars interpret this as God permitting human evil while simultaneously weaving it into His redemptive plan—without being the author of sin.
That means God didn’t approve their wickedness.
But He refused to waste it.
Because we love a God who blesses.
But struggle with a God who builds through breaking.

He spoke too quickly.
Revealed too much.
Wore favor without wisdom.
So God did what love sometimes does.
This was precision training for purpose.
And here’s the truth most people won’t say:

You’re asking God to remove something
He designed to shape you.
And that’s where the story shifts.
Because Joseph is not the hero.
Joseph was betrayed by his brothers.
Jesus was betrayed by His disciple.
Joseph was stripped of his robe.
Jesus was stripped of His garments.
This is where it gets personal.
Because your deepest problem isn’t betrayal.

The pride you protect.
The bitterness you rehearse.
The secret compromises no one sees.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
And sin doesn’t just wound your life.
But God didn’t leave you there.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Jesus didn’t just enter your story.
On the cross, He absorbed the full weight of sin—your sin.

You are more sinful than you admit…
and more loved than you can imagine.
Jesus saves people from eternal separation from God.
So what do you do with this?

The betrayal.
The confusion.
The anger.
The shame.

Not your feelings.
Not your timeline.
Because the same God who turned a pit into a palace…
And if you feel like your life is falling apart right now…
But planted seeds must die to become something greater.
Will you trust Him in the dark?
Will you surrender what you don’t understand?
Will you follow Jesus—not just when it’s easy… but when it costs?
If you’re ready to surrender your life to Jesus,
If this spoke to your situation,
